description: The PAN arm of the H10 project-definition pair: from a one-paragraph product brief, /pan:new-project --auto defines the project (requirements and roadmap), then PAN's autodev loop builds every phase it planned, a fresh Claude Code session per unit, a real model.
why: Program H10, project definition: earlier pairs handed both arms a ready roadmap and requirements, so they measured building, not defining. Here both arms start from the same paragraph (seed brief-shop, BRIEF.md: a stock and order library with reservations, partial shipments, cancellations, low-stock alerts, a daily report and persistence, with several rules that interact) and no .planning/. PAN must turn the brief into requirements and phases itself; the bare host gets the same brief and four fresh sessions with no structure given. Both are judged by the same hidden check (harness/scripts/check-shop.cjs: every behaviour the brief states, the interactions and persistence across restarts). Run both arms together with --repeat N and an approved --max-usd of at least 60 per rep (the run splits it equally between the arms).

pair.goal: Build the product described in the one-paragraph brief BRIEF.md, with tests, across fresh sessions, starting from no project structure.

steps.prompt: /pan:new-project --auto @BRIEF.md (unattended: do not ask questions, take the recommended default and record what you assumed; stop once the requirements and roadmap are committed and do not continue into phase 1, which later sessions build.)
steps.why: new-project defines the project from the brief alone, unattended: a project, requirements and a roadmap of phases. The suffix stops the auto-advance chain at the roadmap, as autodev's own units stop at their command, so every phase is built by the loop in fresh sessions.
autodev runs every phase new-project planned to done, each unit in a fresh session, and the module the brief names exists.
Every behaviour the brief states holds, the interacting rules and persistence across restarts included, judged by a check neither arm saw.
